newsitem.title: ITALY: ISTAT chief sees Italy inflation trend continuing.
newsitem.headline: ISTAT chief sees Italy inflation trend continuing.

text.p: Italy's low inflationary trend is expected to continue, the head of the country's official statistics institute ISTAT, Alberto Zuliani, said on Tuesday.

Zuliani was speaking to reporters on the margins of a conference a day after ISTAT reported March consumer price inflation rose 2.2 percent year-on-year and 0.1 percent month-on-month against 2.4 and 0.1 percent in February.
"The expectation is that the current inflationary trend will be maintained," Zuliani said.

"We can only make a statistical assessment and that is that the month-on-month data in the first quarter of last year where high and from that perspective they should be very high this year but they aren't," he said.
"So the statistical outlook from this point of view is favourable," he said.
Inflation in Italy has fallen steadily over the past year.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said at the weekend that he expected the year-on-year rate would fall to 1.9 percent in April, the lowest since April 1969, and could drop to 1.5 percent by the end of June.
The official government forecast for average annual inflation in 1997 is 2.5 percent.
